--_prose-font-heading-display: var(--_prose-font-heading);"><div class="_blocks_4za3l_47 standard-markdown grid-cols-1 grid [&amp;_&gt;_*]:min-w-0 whitespace-normal break-words print:block standard-markdown"><p dir="ltr"><strong>Why daily QP tasks aren't in the tasks tab:</strong></p>
<p dir="ltr"><code dir="ltr">QbankDailyTaskManager.generateIfNeeded()</code> creates sessions and persists them via <code dir="ltr">CheckmatePrefs</code> (<code dir="ltr">PREF_SESSIONS_JSON</code>), but it never writes a <code dir="ltr">StudyTask</code> into <code dir="ltr">PlanStore</code>. The only place <code dir="ltr">todaysSessions()</code> is read is <code dir="ltr">StatsScreen</code> ("Today's Q-bank Targets" card). Unlike <code dir="ltr">GapTaskManager</code> (which calls into <code dir="ltr">PlanStore</code>/<code dir="ltr">TaskEscrow</code> and shows up on Home), the Q-bank daily target was only ever wired to Stats — it was never supposed to land on the tasks tab in the first place. Not a regression, a missing wire.</p>
<p dir="ltr"><strong>Why phase hand-off won't work as you're picturing it:</strong></p>
<p dir="ltr"><code dir="ltr">ft_schedule</code> (Testmate side) is keyed uniquely by <code dir="ltr">name</code> — <code dir="ltr">PUT /api/qbank/ft-schedule</code> upserts <code dir="ltr">onConflict: 'name'</code>. Phase-4 repeats the same test names (FT-01, FT-02, AIATS-01...) as Phase-3. If you upload the Phase-4 schedule now, each row <strong>overwrites</strong> the matching Phase-3 row immediately — there's no "wait until Phase-3's FT-01 date has passed, then switch" logic, and no <code dir="ltr">phase</code> column at all. <code dir="ltr">daily-target-engine.ts</code> only excludes a test once its <code dir="ltr">test_date</code> is in the past (<code dir="ltr">.gt('test_date', today)</code>); it has zero concept of phases.</p>
<p dir="ltr">So two separate fixes:</p>
<ol dir="ltr">
<li><strong>Tasks tab</strong>: add a step in <code dir="ltr">QbankDailyTaskManager.generateIfNeeded()</code> (or a new small function called from it) that creates a <code dir="ltr">StudyTask</code> per subject session via <code dir="ltr">PlanStore</code>, same pattern <code dir="ltr">GapTaskManager</code> uses — so it shows up on Home instead of only Stats.</li>
<li><strong>Phase hand-off</strong>: give <code dir="ltr">ft_schedule</code> a <code dir="ltr">phase</code> column (or namespace <code dir="ltr">name</code> as <code dir="ltr">"Phase-4:FT-01"</code>), and have <code dir="ltr">computeDailyTarget</code> pick, per test-name, whichever phase's row is the next upcoming one (or fall back to the next phase's row once the current phase's same-named test's <code dir="ltr">test_date</code> has passed) instead of a flat unique-by-name upsert. Requires a migration + a small change to the PUT route and the query in <code dir="ltr">daily-target-engine.ts</code>.</li>
</ol>
<p dir="ltr">Want me to implement both (migration + engine change + Kotlin task wiring), or just one first?</p></div></div></div></div></div></div></div></div></div></div><div class="font-claude-response relative leading-[1.65rem] [&amp;_pre&gt;div]:bg-bg-000/50 [&amp;_pre&gt;div]:border-0.5 [&amp;_pre&gt;div]:border-border-400 [&amp;_.ignore-pre-bg&gt;div]:bg-transparent [&amp;_.progressive-markdown_:is(p,blockquote,h1,h2,h3,h4,h5,h6)]:pl-[var(--msg-text-inset,0.5rem)] [&amp;_.progressive-markdown_:is(p,blockquote,ul,ol,h1,h2,h3,h4,h5,h6)]:pr-8 [&amp;_.md-table-scroll]:pl-[var(--msg-block-inset,0.5rem)] [&amp;_.md-table-scroll]:pr-[var(--msg-inset-end,0.5rem)]"><div data-cds="Prose" class="prose" style="--_prose-font-body: var(--font-claude-response, var(--cds-font-voice)); --_prose-font-heading-display: var(--_prose-font-heading);"><div class="_blocks_4za3l_47 standard-markdown grid-cols-1 grid [&amp;_&gt;_*]:min-w-0 whitespace-normal break-words print:block standard-markdown"><p dir="ltr"><strong>1. Q-bank tasks now show up on your Home tab</strong></p>
<p dir="ltr">Before: when the app auto-created a daily Q-bank practice session (based on your FT schedule), it only showed as a card in the Stats screen. It never became a real task, so it never appeared on Home/tasks.</p>
<p dir="ltr">Now: every time it creates one of these sessions (once per subject, per day), it also drops a real task onto your Home tab — with a duration (~1 min/question) and a "Take test" button that opens straight into that Q-bank session. Same button style you already see on gap-repair and retention-check tasks.</p>
<p dir="ltr"><strong>2. Phase 3 → Phase 4 hand-off</strong></p>
<p dir="ltr">Before: <code dir="ltr">ft_schedule</code> (the table that tells the app which FT/AIATS test is "next" per chapter) only allowed one row per test name. Since Phase-4 reuses the same names (FT-01, FT-02...), uploading Phase-4 would instantly overwrite Phase-3's row — no waiting for Phase-3's test to actually happen first.</p>
<p dir="ltr">Now: Phase-3's "FT-01" and Phase-4's "FT-01" are separate rows (keyed by phase+name). The app already only looks at upcoming (future-dated) tests — so once Phase-3's FT-01 date passes, it drops out automatically and Phase-4's FT-01 (same chapters, later date) takes over as the active driver. No manual switching needed, as long as both rows exist.</p>
<p dir="ltr"><strong>3. Uploading a phase's schedule = one command</strong></p>
<p dir="ltr">Your existing <code dir="ltr">import-questions.ts</code> script now also accepts the richer JSON format (the one with <code dir="ltr">test_name</code>, <code dir="ltr">phase</code>, <code dir="ltr">date</code>, <code dir="ltr">subjects</code>) — same one as your <code dir="ltr">FT-01D_Phase4_NEET2027.json</code>. When you run it with that format, it imports the questions like before, and <strong>also</strong> writes/updates the matching <code dir="ltr">ft_schedule</code> row (phase, date, chapters) in the same step. So there's no separate manual API call to remember.</p>
<p dir="ltr"><strong>4. Fixed the "only Chemistry" bug</strong></p>
<p dir="ltr">That row-writing step now merges chapters with whatever's already there instead of replacing it. So if you import Physics, then Chemistry, then Botany, then Zoology as separate batches for the same test, all four subjects' chapters end up on the row — instead of only the last subject you imported.</p>
<p dir="ltr"><strong>5. <code dir="ltr">tag_source</code> stays <code dir="ltr">manual</code> by default</strong></p>
<p dir="ltr">No behavior change from before on this — regardless of which JSON format you use, it won't tag anything <code dir="ltr">coaching_module</code> unless you explicitly pass that as the tag-source argument.</p></div></div></div></div></div><div data-cds="MessageActions" data-reveal="fade" role="toolbar" aria-label="Message actions" data-size="xs" tabindex="-1" class="flex
